stumbles.quote: Jev will not review declaude_lint's hits on public posts.
stumbles.why: declaude_lint is never explained (what it checks, what a 'hit' is). Jev is also named before it is defined, and 'will not review' is stated before the reasoning.
'tic' is never defined, and register.md is an unexplained file. The reader can't tell what is being classified.
Oskar is unexplained. The question is also about 'implementing Jev' in a process, which the text never describes.

stumbles.quote: It had done well on routing questions
stumbles.why: This refers to earlier work that the text doesn't describe. 'Routing questions' has no context.

stumbles.quote: so at a 5% error budget it could settle only 24.5% of hits
stumbles.why: 'Settle' and 'error budget' are not defined. The reader can't tell how coverage is computed from the probabilities or what is being settled.

stumbles.quote: The bar we set in advance was 50%.
stumbles.why: The 50% bar refers to coverage, but the text doesn't say this clearly, and it is easily confused with the 0.5 threshold.

This base rate is in tension with the per-rule counts that follow (5/44, 5/43, 16/18). Those cover only part of the 261 hits, and the other rules are not shown. It also isn't clear that 'precision' means the share of hits that are tics.

stumbles.quote: At a 0.5 threshold the baseline also beat Jev on accuracy, 0.751 to 0.732.
stumbles.why: The 'also' implies the baseline beat Jev on AUROC, but 0.769 is below Jev's 0.808 with the definition. It only beats the no-definition run (0.697). Which Jev configuration is meant is unclear.

point: Jev, a small calibrated decision model, ranked lint hits only modestly better than a per-category base rate and could settle just 24.5% of hits at a 5% error budget against a 50% bar, so it was not added to the public-post review.
